title: NASA's upside-down parachute switch
caption:
NASA caught pieces of the Sun for over two years, then dropped them on Utah at about 310 km/h. ☀️
A gravity switch meant to sense the capsule slowing and fire the parachute was installed upside down, so the parachute never opened.
Who takes the blame: the one who installed it, or the one who skipped the test?
first_comment: Billions of kilometres of perfect flying, ruined by one part the wrong way up. Every IKEA build ever 🔧
sources: NASA Genesis Mishap Investigation Board report (2006): the capsule's drogue parachute and parafoil did not deploy because the gravity (g) switches were installed in an inverted orientation per an erroneous design; a pre-launch test that would have caught it was not performed
NBC News / AP (2006): the capsule hit the Utah desert on 8 September 2004 at nearly 200 mph (~310 km/h); some solar wind samples were still recovered and studied
NASA Genesis mission: launched August 2001, collected solar wind from December 2001 to April 2004
